speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough going on for over three weeks now. It's mostly dry, but sometimes I cough up a little white phlegm, and I've noticed I get quite short of breath when I try to walk or do any physical activity. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration of over three weeks is concerning; have you experienced any fever, night sweats, or unintended weight loss during this time? Also, do you have a history of smoking or recent exposure to tuberculosis?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't had any fever, night sweats, or lost any weight. I did smoke for 30 years but quit ten years ago, and I don't know anyone with tuberculosis. I want to emphasize that, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is good news regarding the infectious symptoms. Given your history of smoking and the duration of your cough, have you noticed any wheezing or a tightness in your chest? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray REQUEST TEST: Spirometry

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-Ray: Right lower lobe consolidation consistent with a possible pneumonia. No pleural effusion noted. Spirometry: Mild obstructive defect with decreased FEV1/FVC ratio.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Community-Acquired Pneumonia with underlying mild COPD.
